lines.text: A little square tumbles around a big one. Most kids miss a sneaky detail at the corners.
lines.caption: A little square tumbles around a big one. Most kids miss a sneaky detail at the corners.

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's get rolling.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's get rolling.

lines.text: A square with side two is fixed in place.
lines.caption: A square with side two is fixed in place.

lines.text: A square with side one sits on top of it, and their left sides line up.
lines.caption: A square with side one sits on top of it, and their left sides line up.

lines.text: The small square rolls clockwise around the big one, without sliding.
lines.caption: The small square rolls clockwise around the big one, without sliding.

lines.text: Each move turns it about a corner touching the big square, until another side lies flat.
lines.caption: Each move turns it about a corner touching the big square, until another side lies flat.

lines.text: It stops when it first gets back to where it started. How long is the path of the marked corner?
lines.caption: It stops when it first gets back to where it started. How long is the path of the marked corner?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: Which corner do we follow? The one that started on the big square's top left corner. Call it P.
lines.caption: Which corner do we follow? The one that started on the big square's top left corner. Call it P.

lines.text: So P is the small square's BOTTOM left corner. Keep your eye on P.
lines.caption: So P is the small square's BOTTOM left corner. Keep your eye on P.

lines.text: Each move tips the square over a pivot corner. We add up how far P travels on every move.
lines.caption: Each move tips the square over a pivot corner. We add up how far P travels on every move.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

scenes.chapter: Solution 1: one move at a time

lines.text: Welcome back! Our strategy: follow the square one move at a time.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Our strategy: follow the square one move at a time.

lines.text: First move: the square tips over its bottom right corner. That corner is the pivot.
lines.caption: First move: the square tips over its bottom right corner. That corner is the pivot.

lines.text: It makes a quarter turn, ninety degrees, and lands flat on top again.
lines.caption: It makes a quarter turn, ninety degrees, and lands flat on top again.

lines.text: P is one away from the pivot, so P swings along a quarter circle of radius one.
lines.caption: P is one away from the pivot, so P swings along a quarter circle of radius one.

lines.text: A full circle of radius one is two pi long, so a quarter of it is pi over two.
lines.caption: A full circle of radius one is two pi long, so a quarter of it is pi over two.

lines.text: Now the small square sits at the big square's top right corner, and tips over it.
lines.caption: Now the small square sits at the big square's top right corner, and tips over it.

lines.text: After a quarter turn, look! It only touches at one point. No side lies flat yet.
lines.caption: After a quarter turn, look! It only touches at one point. No side lies flat yet.

lines.text: So it keeps going. It needs a half turn, one hundred eighty degrees, to land flat on the right side.
lines.caption: So it keeps going. It needs a half turn, one hundred eighty degrees, to land flat on the right side.

lines.text: How far is P from this pivot? P is across the diagonal of the small square: root two.
lines.caption: How far is P from this pivot? P is across the diagonal of the small square: root two.

lines.text: So P sweeps half a circle of radius root two. That's root two times pi.
lines.caption: So P sweeps half a circle of radius root two. That's root two times pi.

lines.text: Down the right side, another quarter turn. The corner P is one away again, so that's pi over two.
lines.caption: Down the right side, another quarter turn. The corner P is one away again, so that's pi over two.

lines.text: Next, the big square's bottom right corner. Surprise: the pivot IS P! The square flips, and P stays put.
lines.caption: Next, the big square's bottom right corner. Surprise: the pivot IS P! The square flips, and P stays put.

lines.text: That move adds zero. That's half a lap, and the other half repeats the same four moves.
lines.caption: That move adds zero. That's half a lap, and the other half repeats the same four moves.

lines.text: Quarter turn, radius one. Half turn, root two. Quarter turn, radius one. Half turn, zero.
lines.caption: Quarter turn, radius one. Half turn, root two. Quarter turn, radius one. Half turn, zero.

lines.text: P is back at its start, and the square is home. Done!
lines.caption: P is back at its start, and the square is home. Done!

lines.text: Now add it up. Four quarter circles of radius one: four times pi over two, which is two pi.
lines.caption: Now add it up. Four quarter circles of radius one: four times pi over two, which is two pi.

lines.text: Two half circles of radius root two: two times root two pi.
lines.caption: Two half circles of radius root two: two times root two pi.

lines.text: And the two flips around P add nothing, zero.
lines.caption: And the two flips around P add nothing, zero.

lines.text: Total: two plus two root two, all times pi. That's Choice C!
lines.caption: Total: two plus two root two, all times pi. That's Choice C!

lines.text: Here's a slicker way to see the total. Glue the arcs together into whole circles!
lines.caption: Here's a slicker way to see the total. Glue the arcs together into whole circles!

lines.text: Four quarter circles of radius one make one full circle of radius one. That's two pi.
lines.caption: Four quarter circles of radius one make one full circle of radius one. That's two pi.

lines.text: Two half circles of radius root two make one full circle of radius root two. That's two root two pi.
lines.caption: Two half circles of radius root two make one full circle of radius root two. That's two root two pi.

lines.text: One circle plus the other: two pi plus two root two pi. Same answer!
lines.caption: One circle plus the other: two pi plus two root two pi. Same answer!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? When the arcs come in matching sets, like here.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? When the arcs come in matching sets, like here.

lines.text: Now the wrong answers. Each one is a different slip.
lines.caption: Now the wrong answers. Each one is a different slip.

lines.text: Choice A, two plus root two, all times pi, comes from treating each corner move as a quarter turn.
lines.caption: Choice A, two plus root two, all times pi, comes from treating each corner move as a quarter turn.

lines.text: But after a quarter turn the square only touches at a point. It must go on to a half turn.
lines.caption: But after a quarter turn the square only touches at a point. It must go on to a half turn.

lines.text: Choice B, four pi, is what you'd get if you used radius one, not root two, for those half circles.
lines.caption: Choice B, four pi, is what you'd get if you used radius one, not root two, for those half circles.

lines.text: But at the top right corner, P is across the diagonal from the pivot, not along a side.
lines.caption: But at the top right corner, P is across the diagonal from the pivot, not along a side.

lines.text: Choice D, four plus root two, all times pi, is what you'd get if you followed the wrong corner.
lines.caption: Choice D, four plus root two, all times pi, is what you'd get if you followed the wrong corner.

lines.text: That's how far the small square's TOP left corner travels. Our P started at the bottom left.
lines.caption: That's how far the small square's TOP left corner travels. Our P started at the bottom left.

lines.text: Choice E, four plus two root two, all times pi, is what you'd get if the flips around P had radius one.
lines.caption: Choice E, four plus two root two, all times pi, is what you'd get if the flips around P had radius one.

lines.text: But P is the pivot there, so its radius is zero. It doesn't move at all.
lines.caption: But P is the pivot there, so its radius is zero. It doesn't move at all.

lines.text: Wrong angle, wrong radius, wrong corner, forgotten zero. Four slips to watch for!
lines.caption: Wrong angle, wrong radius, wrong corner, forgotten zero. Four slips to watch for!

lines.text: Same squares, same roll, but this time follow the CENTER of the small square. How long is its path?
lines.caption: Same squares, same roll, but this time follow the CENTER of the small square. How long is its path?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. The center is half a diagonal from every corner: root two over two.
lines.caption: Let's check. The center is half a diagonal from every corner: root two over two.

lines.text: So on every move, the center is the same distance from the pivot. No zeros this time!
lines.caption: So on every move, the center is the same distance from the pivot. No zeros this time!

lines.text: Now count the turning: four quarter turns and four half turns.
lines.caption: Now count the turning: four quarter turns and four half turns.

lines.text: Four times ninety plus four times one hundred eighty is one thousand eighty degrees.
lines.caption: Four times ninety plus four times one hundred eighty is one thousand eighty degrees.

lines.text: That's three full turns. So the center travels three full circles of radius root two over two.
lines.caption: That's three full turns. So the center travels three full circles of radius root two over two.

lines.text: Each circle is root two pi long, so the path is three root two pi. Fantastic work!
lines.caption: Each circle is root two pi long, so the path is three root two pi. Fantastic work!

lines.text: In a rolling problem, list every move: its pivot and its angle.
lines.caption: In a rolling problem, list every move: its pivot and its angle.

lines.text: Each point travels an arc whose radius is its distance from the pivot. Sometimes that's zero!
lines.caption: Each point travels an arc whose radius is its distance from the pivot. Sometimes that's zero!

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep rolling, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep rolling, and I'll see you next time!
